speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Health (a) which private insurers cover admission to inpatient hospices as part of their Integrated Shield Plans; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider requiring all private Integrated Shield Plan insurers to cover inpatient hospice admission, just as they presently cover restructured hospital admissions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Together with MediShield Life, the Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are designed mainly to cover large hospital bills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: So, we do have some riders that are covering hospice care today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In assessing whether palliative care should be covered by IPs, we also need to look at whether the services are affordable for most Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH regularly reviews the amount of Government subsidies and MediSave used for hospice care to ensure it remains affordable for patients and also sustainable for providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are also working with community partners to enhance accessibility to palliative care services by increasing capacity for palliative care across the inpatient, home and community settings.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would the Minister of State agree that there is a group of patients who may fall into what some of us term the "sandwich class", who might not qualify for as many subsidies as lower-income patients but, at the same time, would still want to take advantage of the benefits provided by their IPs purchased from the private sector when they were healthy?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would the Minister of State agree that, at the moment, the present system makes it somewhat unfortunate that these patients can access their IP benefits in a restructured hospital but cannot, should they choose to seek end-of-life care at an inpatient hospice?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In addition to Government subsidies, the other important source of support for our patients would be charity dollars.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is an area where we work closely with voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and charities, and they bring more than financial support.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They also bring care and concern, and service from the heart, which is very important for end-of-life care.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The point about IPs and riders, we do have riders that are available, as I explained in my answer.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is something we can review on an ongoing basis to make sure that MediShield Life is able to meet the needs of Singaporeans.
